expected.description: proof-check.sh's no-leading-slash rule misses an option value such as --output=/abs, and allowlist entries accept any trailing words, so a closure proof can point an allowlisted program outside the checkout.
proof-check.sh samples entries in an order fixed by a default seed of 0, so the prover can predict which entries are never checked and place a false one there.
proof-check.sh runs commands without their own process group, so a background child makes a passing command look like a timeout and children keep running after the clone is deleted.
proof-check.sh's isolation rules (environment scrub, HOME isolation, timeout, hooksPath, the ~ refusal, the 200-entry limit and others) have no test that fails when the rule is removed.
